title: Whole Stalked Bell and Perioral Cilia Vorticella
description: One newly authored enlarged generic Vorticella-like ciliate exterior in an extended static pose, one complete model and zero scenes. A slender gently bent uncoiled stalk continuously widens through the aboral attachment into a complete inverted bell zooid. Its broad rolled oral lip, shallow true annular depression and raised closed peristomial disc are continuous parts of the same whole exterior, not an empty decorative cup. Fifty-six whole curved tapered cilia are individually rooted in two schematic oral bands. New complete body profile, stalk course, disc, lip and all ciliary positions; no old rotifer trunk, paired crowns, foot or toes, Paramecium oblong oral groove or distributed somatic rows, fungus cap or held stalked barnacle geometry is reused. The stalk base is only a small natural attachment-end placement datum; no added support, substrate or physical stability claim. Schematic opaque external teaching art, not a measured specimen, exact species, natural dimensions, exact cilium count, taxonomic diagnosis or optical microscopy simulation. Cytostome, internal buccal passage, nuclei, vacuoles and stalk spasmoneme are omitted, not falsely exposed through a hollow cup. No contraction, beating, feeding, water flow, swimming, culture, disease, viability, rig, animation, textures or labels.
